problems.title: GPU Credits

preview_source.scope: group-level public preview; partial; not variant-specific

basis: contentPreview (CreditSystem, out-of-order arrival, revoke at a time, balance at a timestamp)
inference.uncertainty: high: method names, argument order, revoke semantics (per-grant, from t onward) and closed windows are all inferred.

problems.inferred_spec: Grants have unique ids and are valid on the closed window [startTime, endTime]. Events may arrive in any timestamp order; every query reflects all events received so far. revokeCredit(id, t) returns false if the id has not been added yet or was already revoked; otherwise it records that the grant stops counting from time t onward and returns true. getBalance(t) is the sum of amounts of grants with startTime <= t <= endTime that are not revoked at a time <= t.

problems.title: GPU Credits II

preview_source.scope: group-level public preview; partial; not variant-specific

basis: contentPreview (CreditSystem, out-of-order arrival, consume at a time)
inference.uncertainty: high: expiring-first draw order, all-or-nothing consumption, tie-breaks and the replay definition are inferred.

problems.inferred_spec: Grants as in GPU Credits (unique ids, closed windows, out-of-order arrival). The state at time t is defined by replaying all received consumptions with timestamp <= t in (timestamp, arrival) order against the received grants. A consumption at time c succeeds only if the remaining amount of grants active at c is >= amount; it then draws from active grants in order of earliest endTime, then earliest startTime, then creditId ascending; a failing consumption has no effect. consumeCredit returns whether it succeeds in the replay of events received so far (later-arriving earlier events may change later answers). getBalance(t) is the remaining amount of grants active at t after that replay.

problems.title: Generate Random NFT

preview_source.scope: group-level public preview; partial; not variant-specific

basis: contentPreview (trait configuration, one value per trait, duplicates permitted)
inference.uncertainty: medium: modelling randomness as injected integers with modulo selection is an author choice.

problems.inferred_spec: Generate n NFTs with duplicates allowed. For each NFT and each trait in order, take the next random r and choose values[r mod len(values)]. randoms has exactly n * len(traits) entries. Randomness is injected: randoms is a deterministic list of non-negative integers (each <= 10^15) consumed in order. Each NFT is returned as the list of chosen values in trait order.

problems.title: Generate Random NFT

preview_source.scope: group-level public preview; partial; not variant-specific

basis: contentPreview (trait configuration, one value per trait, duplicates permitted)
inference.uncertainty: high: weighted traits are inferred from the BINARY_SEARCH tag only.

problems.inferred_spec: Generate n NFTs with duplicates allowed, where each trait value has a positive integer weight. For each NFT and trait in order, take the next random r, let x = r mod (sum of weights), and choose the first value whose cumulative weight exceeds x. randoms has exactly n * len(traits) entries. Randomness is injected: randoms is a deterministic list of non-negative integers (each <= 10^15) consumed in order. Each NFT is returned as the list of chosen values in trait order.

problems.title: Generate Random NFT

preview_source.scope: group-level public preview; partial; not variant-specific

basis: contentPreview (trait configuration, one value per trait, duplicates permitted)
inference.uncertainty: high: the no-duplicates follow-up is inferred from the preview stressing that duplicates are permitted; the virtual Fisher-Yates model and n > T -> [] are author choices.

problems.inferred_spec: Generate n pairwise-distinct NFTs (uniform sampling without replacement modelled deterministically). Index all T = product(len(values)) combinations in mixed-radix order (first trait most significant, values in given order). Run a partial Fisher-Yates over that virtual array: for i in 0..n-1, swap positions i and i + (randoms[i] mod (T - i)) and emit the combination at position i. If n > T return []. randoms has exactly n entries. Randomness is injected: randoms is a deterministic list of non-negative integers (each <= 10^15) consumed in order. Each NFT is returned as the list of chosen values in trait order.

problems.title: IPO Share Allocation

preview_source.scope: group-level public preview; partial; not variant-specific

basis: contentPreview (bid fields, highest price allocated first)
inference.uncertainty: medium: round-robin by timestamp within a price level and the unallotted-users output follow the widely reported version, not visible preview text.

problems.inferred_spec: Each user bids once. Shares go to price levels from highest to lowest. If a level's total requested shares fit in the remaining shares, every bidder there receives their full request. Otherwise the remaining shares are handed out one at a time round-robin over that level's bidders ordered by timestamp (ties by input order), skipping bidders already satisfied, until shares run out. Return the sorted userIds that receive zero shares.
